title: Path Store That Needs a Parent
statement:
Build a tiny store that maps slash-separated paths such as /app/src/main to integer values. A path is one or more segments of lowercase letters, each preceded by /.

  • PathStore() creates an empty store. Only the invisible root exists.
  • create(path, value) adds path with value and returns true. It returns false and changes nothing if the path already exists, or if its parent path does not exist. The parent of /app/src is /app; the parent of a one-segment path like /app is the root, which always exists.
  • get(path) returns the value stored at path, or -1 if there is none.

Tests are a list of operations and their arguments; the first creates the store. The expected output has one entry per operation (null for the constructor).

examples.why: /app/src succeeds because /app was created first. /lib/x fails: /lib was never created.
Creating an existing path does not overwrite it.
"/ab" starts with the characters "/a", but it is not the path /a. The parent must match whole segments.

hints: Every path is unique, so a hash map from the full path string to its value already answers get. What does create need to check?
The parent of a path is everything before its last slash. For a one-segment path that prefix is the empty string, meaning the root.
A trie of segments works too: walk the segments, fail if a parent segment is missing, and add a node only for the last one.

explain.intuition:
This is the core of a router or a nested settings object: a key is valid only if its parent key exists. Because the full path identifies a node, a single hash map from path to value is enough. create cuts the path at its last / to get the parent, checks that the parent exists (or is the root), checks that the path itself is new, and stores it.

A trie keyed by segment is the more structural answer and what interviewers often expect: each node has a map of child segments. Walking the segments one by one gives the parent check for free, and it also makes follow-ups like "list all children" easy.
steps: Keep a map values from full path to value.
create(path, value): if path is already in the map, return false.
Let parent = path.slice(0, path.lastIndexOf('/')). If parent is not empty and not in the map, return false.
pitfalls: Checking the parent with a string prefix test. /ab starts with /a but is not its child.
Overwriting the value when the path already exists. create must fail instead.
Creating missing parents automatically, like mkdir -p. Here a missing parent makes the call fail.

complexity.time: O(L) per call, L = path length

solutions.title: Hash map of full paths
solutions.idea: The parent is the path up to the last slash. Check that it exists, check that the path is new, then store.

solutions.title: Trie of segments
solutions.idea: Each node maps a segment name to a child node. Walk all segments but the last; every one must exist. The last one must not.

followups: Add delete(path) that removes a path and everything under it. Which solution makes this cheap?
Add a watcher: watch(path, callback) fires whenever something is created at or below that path.
